+# API Integration
+
+## Base URL
+
+Single source of truth: `lib/core/config/app_config.dart` — feature code
+never holds URLs.
+
+1. `--dart-define=API_BASE_URL=…` (any build: staging / LAN device)
+2. Release builds → `https://guides-nepal.onrender.com/api/v1` (verified
+   production API)
+3. Debug builds → `10.0.2.2:8000` (Android emulator) or `localhost:8000`
+   (iOS simulator / desktop)
+
+Cleartext HTTP exists **only** for dev hosts and debug builds
+(`android/app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml`; the manifest
+sets `android:usesCleartextTraffic="false"`). iOS ATS stays at platform
+default (blocks arbitrary cleartext); use the simulator's localhost or HTTPS.
+
+## Client
+
+One Dio instance (`ApiClient`, `lib/core/network/api_client.dart`):
+
+- Timeouts: connect 15 s · receive 30 s · send 20 s.
+- `AuthInterceptor` attaches `Authorization: Bearer …` (cached token, async
+  secure-storage fallback), and fires `onUnauthorized` on any 401 so the
+  session ends app-wide.
+- Every `DioException` is normalized exactly once by
+  `ApiClient.mapDioException` → `ApiException(kind, statusCode, message,
+  fieldErrors)`. FastAPI 422 payloads become `{field: message}`.
+- **No automatic retries.** Reads may be re-fetched via UI retry buttons;
+  `POST /bookings/` is never retried — the booking flow guards with
+  `_submitting`/`_submitted` flags so double-taps can't duplicate bookings.
+- Requests carry `CancelToken`s; Explore cancels in-flight searches when
+  filters change.
+
+## Authentication
+
+| Flow | Endpoint | Notes |
+|---|---|---|
+| Register | `POST /auth/register` | sends `role: traveler` (backend allow-lists) |
+| Login | `POST /auth/login` | returns `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `user` |
+| Session | `GET /profile/me` | validates stored session on startup |
+| Logout | local | clears secure storage + cached token (server has no revocation endpoint) |
+| Password | `POST /auth/change-password` | wired in `AuthRepository` |
+| OAuth | — | backend redirects OAuth callbacks to the **web** frontend; not usable from mobile without backend changes (see api-gaps.md) |
+
+Tokens are stored **only** in `flutter_secure_storage` (Keychain /
+EncryptedSharedPreferences), never in SharedPreferences or logs.
+
+## Endpoint map (all verified against `backend/app/api/v1/`)
+
+```
+GET    /experiences?city&category&search&min_price&max_price&sort
+GET    /experiences/{slug}
+GET    /guides?city            GET /guides/{id}
+GET    /reviews/?experience_id GET /reviews/can-review   POST /reviews/
+GET    /bookings/availability?date
+GET    /bookings/              POST /bookings/
+POST   /bookings/{id}/cancel   POST /bookings/{id}/archive
+GET    /profile/me             PATCH /profile/me
+GET    /profile/bookmarks      POST /profile/bookmarks   DELETE /profile/bookmarks/{id}
+POST   /ai/chat                POST /ai/chat/stream
+GET    /guide/me               GET /guide/dashboard      GET /guide/bookings
+PATCH  /guide/bookings/{id}    GET /guide/listings        PATCH /guide/listings/{id}/capacity
+GET|PUT /guide/onboarding      POST /guide/status         DELETE /guide/status/{id}
+POST   /auth/register|login|change-password|forgot-password
+```
+
+## Models
+
+`lib/shared/models/` — parsers are defensive (`as num? ?? fallback`,
+`is Map` checks) because seeded content rows omit optional fields that live
+host rows include. Unknown/missing booking status falls back to `upcoming`
+rather than throwing.
+
+## Currency
+
+Prices are displayed exactly as the backend's booking currency (USD,
+`Formatters.bookingCurrency*`) and labeled `/ person` — no exchange-rate
+conversion is ever invented client-side.

+# Architecture
+
+## Stack
+
+Flutter 3.47 / Dart 3.13 · Riverpod (state) · GoRouter (navigation) ·
+Dio (HTTP) · flutter_secure_storage (credentials).
+
+## Layers
+
+Feature-first; each feature holds only the layers it needs:
+
+```
+Screen (ConsumerWidget/StatefulWidget)
+  └─► Controller / provider (Riverpod Notifier, FutureProvider, StateNotifier)
+        └─► Repository (contract-typed API access)
+              └─► ApiClient (single Dio instance + AuthInterceptor)
+                    └─► Backend /api/v1
+```
+
+- **Presentation** — widgets never call Dio directly; they watch providers and
+  call controllers. All copy comes from `lib/l10n/app_strings.dart`.
+- **State** — Riverpod only. Global session lives in
+  `authControllerProvider`; per-screen data uses `FutureProvider.autoDispose`
+  families (e.g. `experienceDetailProvider(slug)`).
+- **Data** — repositories translate verified backend contracts into typed
+  models (`lib/shared/models/`). Parsing is defensive: optional server fields
+  never crash a screen.
+
+## State management
+
+| Kind                  | Used for                                   |
+|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------|
+| `Notifier`            | session (`AuthState`), favorites mirror    |
+| `StateNotifier`       | Explore filters (search/city/category)     |
+| `FutureProvider`      | all reads (experiences, trips, dashboard…) |
+| `StateProvider`       | tiny ephemeral UI state (debounced search) |
+
+Optimistic updates are used only for favorites, with automatic revert if the
+server rejects — a save that failed is never shown as saved.
+
+## Navigation
+
+`lib/app/router/app_router.dart` — GoRouter with a `redirect` guard:
+
+1. `AuthStatus.restoring` → hold on `/splash` (session validated against
+   `GET /profile/me`).
+2. Signed out → only `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/onboarding`, `/splash`.
+3. Signed in → `/sign-in|/sign-up` bounce to `/home`.
+4. **Role guard**: `/guide*` requires `role == 'guide'`; travelers are
+   redirected to `/home`. The backend still enforces authorization on every
+   guide endpoint (`require_role`), the guard is UX only.
+
+Five-tab `StatefulShellRoute` (Home · Explore · Trips · Inbox · Profile) plus
+full-screen routes: experience detail, guide profile, destination, booking
+flow, Maila Dai, saved.
+
+## Data flow (example: booking)
+
+```
+BookingFlow → availability GET /bookings/availability?date=…
+           → POST /bookings/ (single non-idempotent call,
+             guarded by _submitting/_submitted flags — no auto-retry)
+           → invalidate bookingsProvider → Trips shows server truth
+```
+
+## Error model
+
+`ApiException` with `ApiFailureKind` (network, unauthorized, forbidden,
+notFound, validation, server, canceled, unknown). `ApiClient.mapDioException`
+maps every Dio failure once; UI switches on `kind` and shows friendly copy —
+backend traces are never rendered.
+
+## Offline / resilience
+
+- Loading → skeleton, never a bare spinner or blank screen.
+- Every list has empty + error + retry states.
+- Search is debounced (350 ms) and in-flight requests are canceled on filter
+  change, so rapid typing can't race stale responses.
+- Session restore falls back to the cached identity on network failure
+  instead of logging the user out spuriously; a real 401 clears storage and
+  ends the session everywhere (`AuthInterceptor.onUnauthorized`).

+# Design System
+
+Tokens live in `lib/app/theme/` (`app_colors.dart`, `app_spacing.dart`,
+`app_typography.dart`, `app_theme.dart`); components in `lib/shared/widgets/`.
+
+## Brand colors
+
+Derived from the website's Tailwind theme so site and app share one identity.
+
+| Token | Hex | Use |
+|---|---|---|
+| primary | `#213448` | deep Himalayan blue — headings, dark surfaces |
+| secondary | `#547792` | medium blue — secondary elements, links |
+| tertiary | `#94B4C1` | mist blue — placeholders, subdued icons |
+| accent | `#F4B400` | brand yellow — primary CTA fill (with `#213448` text) |
+| background | `#FDF8F5` | warm cream app background |
+| surface | `#FFFFFF` | cards, sheets, input fills |
+| surfacePeach / peach | `#FFF0E6` / `#F9E6D6` | warm highlights, chips, hero |
+| border | `#E7E1D8` | warm hairline borders |
+| textPrimary / Secondary / Tertiary | `#213448` / `#667085` / `#98A2B3` | type hierarchy |
+| success / error / warning | `#1E7B4F` / `#C0392B` / `#B7791F` | status (+ tinted surfaces) |
+| favoriteActive | `#E0475B` | saved heart |
+
+No pure black anywhere; white is used for cards only, not as page
+background. No decorative gradients — the Home hero and destination header
+use the two brand blues as an editorial block.
+
+## Typography
+
+- **PlayfairDisplay** (bundled, SIL OFL) — editorial display: `displayLarge/Medium/Small`.
+- **Inter** (bundled, SIL OFL) — all UI: `h1–h3`, `title`, `subtitle`, `body`,
+  `small`, `caption`, `label`, `overline`, plus numeric `price`/`priceLarge`.
+
+Variable-font `wght` axis set explicitly via `FontVariation`. Never hardcode
+font sizes in screens — always use `AppTypography.*`.
+
+## Spacing & radii
+
+Scale: `4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64` (`AppSpacing.x1…x16`),
+`gutter = 20` for screen padding, `minTouchTarget = 44`.
+
+Radii: `sm 8` (inputs, small images) · `md 12` (buttons, fields, list tiles) ·
+`lg 16` (cards) · `xl 20` (hero blocks, dialogs) · `pill 999` (chips,
+search). Buttons are 12, cards 16 — nothing is a pill by default.
+
+## Components (`lib/shared/widgets/`)
+
+| Component | States / notes |
+|---|---|
+| `AppButton` | primary (yellow) / secondary (blue) / outline / ghost; **loading** state blocks double-submit; min 44dp targets; `expanded` |
+| `AppTextField` | label, error text, password reveal toggle, semantics |
+| `ExperienceCard` | 4:3 image, save heart (never covers title), meta line, rating row, per-person price; accessible label reads title/city/rating/price |
+| `GuideCard` / `GuideAvatar` | portrait with initials fallback |
+| `NetworkImageView` | cache + shimmer placeholder + error fallback, `maxWidthDiskCache: 1600` |
+| `SectionHeader` | title + optional action |
+| `AppFilterChip` / `InfoChip` | selected + unselected |
+| `SkeletonBox` / `SkeletonList` | shimmer loading (respects reduced motion) |
+| `EmptyStateView` / `ErrorStateView` | icon + copy + optional action / retry |
+
+Interactions: hearts animate and reconcile with the server; bottom sheets and
+dialogs come from the theme; `pageTransitionsTheme` uses Cupertino
+transitions on **both** platforms for a native feel. Animations are disabled
+under reduced-motion (`MediaQuery.disableAnimationsOf`).
+
+## Accessibility
+
+- Touch targets ≥ 44dp (`minTouchTarget`), navigation bar height 64.
+- Screen-reader semantics on cards, hearts, images, buttons.
+- Text scaling left at system default; type uses `height` for reflow.
+- Contrast: `#213448` on cream/white ≥ 7:1; CTA is `#213448` on `#F4B400`.
+- Light theme only — dark mode ships only when it can be done coherently
+  (documented decision, not an oversight).
+
+## Conventions
+
+All user-facing copy lives in `AppStrings` — no literal UI strings in
+widgets. Status chips map booking states → color pairs in one place per
+screen family.

+# Build & Release
+
+## Environment configuration
+
+| Build | API base | Cleartext |
+|---|---|---|
+| Debug (emulator/device) | auto: `10.0.2.2:8000` / `localhost:8000` | dev hosts only (Android network security config) |
+| Any build + `--dart-define=API_BASE_URL=…` | your override | only if override is `http://` **and** it's a dev host |
+| Release | `https://guides-nepal.onrender.com/api/v1` | never |
+

+# Security & Privacy
+
+## Credential storage
+
+- Tokens live **only** in `flutter_secure_storage`:
+  **iOS Keychain**, **Android EncryptedSharedPreferences**
+  (`lib/core/storage/token_storage.dart`).
+- Never in SharedPreferences/plain files, never in the source tree, never in
+  logs. `AuthInterceptor` attaches the header from memory/cache; it never
+  prints request or response bodies.
+- Passwords are only ever typed into login/register forms — never stored,
+  never logged, never put in URLs.
+- Logout clears the whole session (access + refresh + cached user JSON) and
+  the in-memory header.
+
+## Transport
+
+- **Production is HTTPS-only**: release builds resolve
+  `https://guides-nepal.onrender.com/api/v1`; TLS verification is never
+  disabled and no certificate-pinning bypass exists.
+- Android `network_security_config.xml`: `cleartextTrafficPermitted="false"`
+  base config; cleartext allowed **only** for `10.0.2.2`, `localhost`,
+  `127.0.0.1` (dev backends). The manifest additionally sets
+  `android:usesCleartextTraffic="false"`.
+- iOS App Transport Security is left at the platform default (no arbitrary
+  HTTP). Debug against the simulator's localhost or an HTTPS host.
+- Dev URL overrides are explicit (`--dart-define=API_BASE_URL`), so a
+  release build cannot silently point at an HTTP host: `AppConfig.baseUrl`
+  returns the production HTTPS URL whenever `kReleaseMode`.
+
+## Authorization model
+
+- The app performs **no client-side privilege decisions** — role guards in
+  the router are UX only. Every guide endpoint is `require_role("guide")`
+  and scoped server-side to the authenticated user's id; booking queries are
+  scoped to the token's user.
+- No client-supplied ids are trusted for another user's data: favorites and
+  trips are always read/written under the session's own token.
+- Registration is hard-coded to `role: traveler` — no client role escalation.
+
+## Error handling
+
+- All failures map to `ApiException`; screens show friendly copy.
+  Backend stack traces / `detail` payloads are never rendered raw.
+- A global 401 handler ends the session instead of looping on expired
+  credentials.
+
+## Privacy & permissions
+
+- Android permissions: `INTERNET` only — no camera, location, contacts or
+  storage permissions are requested (nothing in the current feature set
+  needs them).
+- Data collected: account email/name, profile fields the user edits, their
+  bookings/favorites, and chat content with Maila Dai. Nothing is shared
+  with third-party analytics or crash SDKs (no such dependency exists in
+  `pubspec.yaml`).
+- No secrets or API keys are embedded in the app bundle — the AI assistant
+  calls the backend proxy (`/ai/chat`), whose keys stay server-side.
+
+## Platform notes
+
+- `url_launcher` is declared for external links; any future external link
+  must use `https://` only.
+- If uploads are ever added: validate type/size client-side and re-validate
+  server-side (the current profile flow does not upload files).

+flutter build apk --debug

+
+## Unit tests (`test/widget_test.dart`)
+
+1. **Brand copy** — `AppStrings` exposes the canonical product strings.
+2. **Formatters** — whole vs decimal prices (`$50`, `$49.50`),
+   `/ person` suffix, singular/plural review + guest counts (this is the
+   booking price display contract).
+3. **Booking status** — parses every server value, falls back to `upcoming`
+   on unknown/null instead of throwing; `canCancel` is true only for
+   `upcoming`/`accepted` (drives cancellation UI).
+4. **Experience parsing (populated row)** — id/slug/title/price/rating/
+   reviews/city/category plus nested host with languages & verified flag.
+5. **Experience parsing (minimal row)** — seeded rows without optional
+   fields parse to nulls/defaults rather than crashing.
+
+## What's deliberately mocked vs real
+
+Tests are hermetic: pure Dart parsing/formatting only — no live backend, no
+network, no production accounts. Repositories take an injected `ApiClient`,
+so HTTP can be faked later without touching screens.
+

+- Router redirect-guard tests (signed-out bounce, traveler → `/guide`
+  bounce) — the logic lives in one `redirect` closure, ready to unit-test
+  with a fake `AuthState`.
+- Integration tests (`integration_test/`) for startup → sign-in → explore →
+  detail → booking: needs a seeded local backend; not run here.
+
+These are honest gaps; none of the passing claims above substitute for them.
+
+## Regression rules
+
+- Never delete or weaken a test to make a change pass.
+- Every fix must keep `flutter analyze` at zero and `flutter test` green.

class _FakeTripsApi extends ApiClient {
  _FakeTripsApi(List<Map<String, dynamic>> bookings) : _store = bookings.map((b) => Map<String,dynamic>.of(b)).toList();
  final List<Map<String, dynamic>> _store;
  final List<String> requests = [];  // e.g. 'POST /bookings/1/cancel'
  Completer<void>? cancelGate;
  ApiException? cancelError;
  ApiException? archiveError;

  @override
  Future<Response<dynamic>> get(String path, {query, cancelToken}) async {
    if (path == '/bookings/') return _ok(_store.map((b) => Map.of(b)).toList());
    throw notFound;
  }

  @override
  Future<Response<dynamic>> post(String path, {data, cancelToken}) async {
    requests.add('POST $path');
    final m = RegExp(r'^/bookings/(\d+)/(cancel|archive)$').firstMatch(path);
    if (m != null) {
      final id = int.parse(m.group(1)!);
      final action = m.group(2)!;
      if (action == 'cancel') {
        final gate = cancelGate; if (gate != null) await gate.future;
        final err = cancelError; if (err != null) throw err;
      } else {
        final err = archiveError; if (err != null) throw err;
      }
      final idx = _store.indexWhere((b) => b['id'] == id);
      if (idx == -1) throw ApiException(notFound...);
      _store[idx] = {..._store[idx], 'status': action == 'cancel' ? 'cancelled' : 'archived'};
      return _ok(Map.of(_store[idx]));
    }
    throw notFound;
  }
}
```

/// Minimal signed-in session for the Trips tab.
class _FakeAuthController extends AuthController {
  @override
  AuthState build() => const AuthState(
        status: AuthStatus.authenticated,
      );
}

Map<String, dynamic> _bookingJson({
  required int id,
  required String title,
  required String status,
  String city = 'Pokhara',
  int guests = 2,
  double price = 200,
}) =>
    {
      'id': id,
      'experience_id': 7,
      'experience_title': title,
      'city': city,
      'date': '2026-11-02T00:00:00Z',
      'guests': guests,
      'price': price,
      'status': status,
      'user_id': 11,
      'created_at': '2026-10-21T09:00:00Z',
      'image': null,
    };

/// Scripted transport for the trips list plus the cancel/archive actions.
/// The fake holds the server-side list and mutates it on cancel/archive,
/// so a refetch after the action reflects the real state transition.
class _FakeTripsApi extends ApiClient {
  _FakeTripsApi(this._server);

  List<Map<String, dynamic>> _server;

  final List<String> postedPaths = [];

  /// When set, the matching POST parks until the completer completes.
  Completer<void>? actionGate;
  ApiException? actionError;

  List<Map<String, dynamic>> get server => _server;

  @override
  Future<Response<dynamic>> get(
    String path, {
    Map<String, dynamic>? query,
    CancelToken? cancelToken,
  }) async {
    if (path == '/bookings/') {
      return _ok(_server.map((b) => Map<String, dynamic>.of(b)).toList());
    }
    throw ApiException(kind: ApiFailureKind.notFound, message: 'Unexpected GET $path');
  }

  @override
  Future<Response<dynamic>> post(
    String path, {
    Object? data,
    CancelToken? cancelToken,
  }) async {
    postedPaths.add(path);
    final match = RegExp(r'^/bookings/(\d+)/(cancel|archive)$').firstMatch(path);
    if (match == null) {
      throw ApiException(kind: ApiFailureKind.notFound, message: 'Unexpected POST $path');
    }
    final gate = actionGate;
    if (gate != null) await gate.future;
    final error = actionError;
    if (error != null) throw error;

    final id = int.parse(match.group(1)!);
    final action = match.group(2)!;
    final index = _server.indexWhere((b) => b['id'] == id);
    if (index == -1) {
      throw ApiException(kind: ApiFailureKind.notFound, message: 'Booking not found');
    }
    _server[index] = {
      ..._server[index],
      'status': action == 'cancel' ? 'cancelled' : 'archived',
    };
    return _ok(Map<String, dynamic>.of(_server[index]));
  }

  Response<dynamic> _ok(Object data) =>
      Response(data: data, requestOptions: RequestOptions(path: '/'));
}

/// Cancel/archive actions on the Trips tab, against a mocked API layer.
/// The list and both actions run through the real `BookingRepository`
/// and `Booking.fromJson`, so the status transitions verified here are
/// the ones the backend contract defines.
void main() {
  late _FakeTripsApi fake;
  late GoRouter router;

  Future<void> pumpTrips(
    WidgetTester tester, {
    List<Map<String, dynamic>>? server,
  }) async {
    fake = _FakeTripsApi(server ??
        [
          _bookingJson(id: 1, title: 'Sunrise over Sarangkot', status: 'upcoming'),
          _bookingJson(id: 2, title: 'Bhaktapur food walk', status: 'completed'),
        ]);
    router = GoRouter(
      initialLocation: '/trips',
      routes: [
        GoRoute(path: '/trips', builder: (_, __) => const TripsScreen()),
        GoRoute(
          path: '/explore',
          builder: (_, __) => const Scaffold(body: Text('explore-screen')),
        ),
      ],
    );
    await tester.pumpWidget(
      ProviderScope(
        overrides: [
          apiClientProvider.overrideWithValue(fake),
          authControllerProvider.overrideWith(_FakeAuthController.new),
        ],
        child: MaterialApp.router(routerConfig: router),
      ),
    );
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
  }

  Future<void> drainSnackbars(WidgetTester tester) async {
    await tester.pump(const Duration(seconds: 5));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
  }

  /// Taps the tile's action and confirms the cancellation dialog.
  Future<void> cancelFirstTrip(WidgetTester tester) async {
    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Cancel trip'));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(FilledButton, 'Cancel trip'));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
  }

  testWidgets('live trips offer cancel; terminal trips offer archive',
      (tester) async {
    await pumpTrips(tester);

    expect(find.text('Sunrise over Sarangkot'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(find.text('UPCOMING'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(find.text('Bhaktapur food walk'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(find.text('COMPLETED'), findsOneWidget);

    // One action per tile, matched to the booking's state.
    final cancelButtons = find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Cancel trip');
    final archiveButtons = find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Archive');
    expect(cancelButtons, findsOneWidget);
    expect(archiveButtons, findsOneWidget);
    expect(fake.postedPaths, isEmpty);
  });

  testWidgets('cancelling asks for confirmation first', (tester) async {
    await pumpTrips(tester);

    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Cancel trip'));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();

    expect(find.text('Cancel this trip?'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(fake.postedPaths, isEmpty); // nothing sent yet

    // Backing out leaves everything untouched.
    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(TextButton, 'Keep trip'));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();

    expect(find.text('UPCOMING'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(fake.postedPaths, isEmpty);
    expect(fake.server.first['status'], 'upcoming');
  });

  testWidgets('confirmed cancellation posts, refreshes and flips the chip',
      (tester) async {
    await pumpTrips(tester);

    await cancelFirstTrip(tester);

    expect(fake.postedPaths, ['/bookings/1/cancel']);
    // The refetch returns the server's new state — tile now reads cancelled.
    expect(find.text('CANCELLED'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(find.text('UPCOMING'), findsNothing);
    // A cancelled trip offers archive, not cancel.
    expect(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Archive'), findsNWidgets(2));
    expect(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Cancel trip'), findsNothing);
  });

  testWidgets('archive clears a terminal trip to ARCHIVED', (tester) async {
    await pumpTrips(tester);

    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Archive'));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();

    expect(fake.postedPaths, ['/bookings/2/archive']);
    expect(find.text('ARCHIVED'), findsOneWidget);
    // Archived tiles show no further actions.
    expect(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Archive'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Cancel trip'), findsOneWidget);
  });

  testWidgets('a failed cancel keeps the trip and surfaces the error',
      (tester) async {
    await pumpTrips(tester);
    fake.actionError = ApiException(
      kind: ApiFailureKind.server,
      statusCode: 500,
      message: 'Guides Nepal is having trouble right now. Please try again.',
    );

    await cancelFirstTrip(tester);

    expect(
      find.text('Guides Nepal is having trouble right now. Please try again.'),
      findsOneWidget,
    );
    // Unchanged on screen and on the server.
    expect(find.text('UPCOMING'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(fake.server.first['status'], 'upcoming');
    await drainSnackbars(tester);

    // Retry succeeds once the server recovers.
    fake.actionError = null;
    await cancelFirstTrip(tester);
    expect(find.text('CANCELLED'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(fake.postedPaths, hasLength(2));
  });

  testWidgets('only one action request leaves the app while in flight',
      (tester) async {
    await pumpTrips(tester);
    final gate = Completer<void>();
    fake.actionGate = gate;

    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Cancel trip'));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(FilledButton, 'Cancel trip'));
    await tester.pump();
    expect(fake.postedPaths, ['/bookings/1/cancel']);

    // The tile's button is in its loading state; a second tap is a no-op.
    expect(
      tester
          .widget<AppButton>(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Cancel trip').first)
          .loading,
      isTrue,
    );
    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Cancel trip').first);
    await tester.pump();

    gate.complete();
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();

    expect(fake.postedPaths, ['/bookings/1/cancel']); // still exactly one
    expect(find.text('CANCELLED'), findsOneWidget);
  });

  testWidgets('empty trips state invites the traveler to explore',
      (tester) async {
    await pumpTrips(tester, server: []);

    expect(find.text('No trips booked yet'), findsOneWidget);

    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, AppStrings.exploreExperiences));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    expect(find.text('explore-screen'), findsOneWidget);
  });
}

+import 'dart:async';
+
+import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+import 'package:flutter_riverpod/flutter_riverpod.dart';
+import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
+import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';
+
+import 'package:guides_nepal/core/network/api_client.dart';
+import 'package:guides_nepal/core/network/api_exception.dart';
+import 'package:guides_nepal/features/auth/auth_controller.dart';
+import 'package:guides_nepal/features/trips/trips_screen.dart';
+import 'package:guides_nepal/l10n/app_strings.dart';
+import 'package:guides_nepal/shared/widgets/widgets.dart';
+
+/// Minimal signed-in session for the Trips tab.
+class _FakeAuthController extends AuthController {
+  @override
+  AuthState build() => const AuthState(
+        status: AuthStatus.authenticated,
+      );
+}
+
+Map<String, dynamic> _bookingJson({
+  required int id,
+  required String title,
+  required String status,
+  String city = 'Pokhara',
+  int guests = 2,
+  double price = 200,
+}) =>
+    {
+      'id': id,
+      'experience_id': 7,
+      'experience_title': title,
+      'city': city,
+      'date': '2026-11-02T00:00:00Z',
+      'guests': guests,
+      'price': price,
+      'status': status,
+      'user_id': 11,
+      'created_at': '2026-10-21T09:00:00Z',
+      'image': null,
+    };
+
+/// Scripted transport for the trips list plus the cancel/archive actions.
+/// The fake holds the server-side list and mutates it on cancel/archive,
+/// so a refetch after the action reflects the real state transition.
+class _FakeTripsApi extends ApiClient {
+  _FakeTripsApi(this._server);
+
+  final List<Map<String, dynamic>> _server;
+
+  final List<String> postedPaths = [];
+
+  /// When set, the matching POST parks until the completer completes.
+  Completer<void>? actionGate;
+  ApiException? actionError;
+
+  List<Map<String, dynamic>> get server => _server;
+
+  @override
+  Future<Response<dynamic>> get(
+    String path, {
+    Map<String, dynamic>? query,
+    CancelToken? cancelToken,
+  }) async {
+    if (path == '/bookings/') {
+      return _ok(_server.map((b) => Map<String, dynamic>.of(b)).toList());
+    }
+    throw ApiException(kind: ApiFailureKind.notFound, message: 'Unexpected GET $path');
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Future<Response<dynamic>> post(
+    String path, {
+    Object? data,
+    CancelToken? cancelToken,
+  }) async {
+    postedPaths.add(path);
+    final match = RegExp(r'^/bookings/(\d+)/(cancel|archive)$').firstMatch(path);
+    if (match == null) {
+      throw ApiException(kind: ApiFailureKind.notFound, message: 'Unexpected POST $path');
+    }
+    final gate = actionGate;
+    if (gate != null) await gate.future;
+    final error = actionError;
+    if (error != null) throw error;
+
+    final id = int.parse(match.group(1)!);
+    final action = match.group(2)!;
+    final index = _server.indexWhere((b) => b['id'] == id);
+    if (index == -1) {
+      throw ApiException(kind: ApiFailureKind.notFound, message: 'Booking not found');
+    }
+    _server[index] = {
+      ..._server[index],
+      'status': action == 'cancel' ? 'cancelled' : 'archived',
+    };
+    return _ok(Map<String, dynamic>.of(_server[index]));
+  }
+
+  Response<dynamic> _ok(Object data) =>
+      Response(data: data, requestOptions: RequestOptions(path: '/'));
+}
+
+/// Cancel/archive actions on the Trips tab, against a mocked API layer.
+/// The list and both actions run through the real `BookingRepository`
+/// and `Booking.fromJson`, so the status transitions verified here are
+/// the ones the backend contract defines.
+void main() {
+  late _FakeTripsApi fake;
+  late GoRouter router;
+
+  Future<void> pumpTrips(
+    WidgetTester tester, {
+    List<Map<String, dynamic>>? server,
+  }) async {
+    fake = _FakeTripsApi(server ??
+        [
+          _bookingJson(id: 1, title: 'Sunrise over Sarangkot', status: 'upcoming'),
+          _bookingJson(id: 2, title: 'Bhaktapur food walk', status: 'completed'),
+        ]);
+    router = GoRouter(
+      initialLocation: '/trips',
+      routes: [
+        GoRoute(path: '/trips', builder: (_, __) => const TripsScreen()),
+        GoRoute(
+          path: '/explore',
+          builder: (_, __) => const Scaffold(body: Text('explore-screen')),
+        ),
+      ],
+    );
+    await tester.pumpWidget(
+      ProviderScope(
+        overrides: [
+          apiClientProvider.overrideWithValue(fake),
+          authControllerProvider.overrideWith(_FakeAuthController.new),
+        ],
+        child: MaterialApp.router(routerConfig: router),
+      ),
+    );
+    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
+  }
+
+  Future<void> drainSnackbars(WidgetTester tester) async {
+    await tester.pump(const Duration(seconds: 5));
+    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
+  }
+
+  /// Taps the tile's action and confirms the cancellation dialog.
+  Future<void> cancelFirstTrip(WidgetTester tester) async {
+    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Cancel trip'));
+    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
+    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(FilledButton, 'Cancel trip'));
+    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
+  }
+
+  testWidgets('live trips offer cancel; terminal trips offer archive',
+      (tester) async {
+    await pumpTrips(tester);
+
+    expect(find.text('Sunrise over Sarangkot'), findsOneWidget);
+    expect(find.text('UPCOMING'), findsOneWidget);
+    expect(find.text('Bhaktapur food walk'), findsOneWidget);
+    expect(find.text('COMPLETED'), findsOneWidget);
+
+    // One action per tile, matched to the booking's state.
+    final cancelButtons = find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Cancel trip');
+    final archiveButtons = find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Archive');
+    expect(cancelButtons, findsOneWidget);
+    expect(archiveButtons, findsOneWidget);
+    expect(fake.postedPaths, isEmpty);
+  });
+
+  testWidgets('cancelling asks for confirmation first', (tester) async {
+    await pumpTrips(tester);
+
+    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Cancel trip'));
+    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
+
+    expect(find.text('Cancel this trip?'), findsOneWidget);
+    expect(fake.postedPaths, isEmpty); // nothing sent yet
+
+    // Backing out leaves everything untouched.
+    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(TextButton, 'Keep trip'));
+    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
+
+    expect(find.text('UPCOMING'), findsOneWidget);
+    expect(fake.postedPaths, isEmpty);
+    expect(fake.server.first['status'], 'upcoming');
+  });
+
+  testWidgets('confirmed cancellation posts, refreshes and flips the chip',
+      (tester) async {
+    await pumpTrips(tester);
+
+    await cancelFirstTrip(tester);
+
+    expect(fake.postedPaths, ['/bookings/1/cancel']);
+    // The refetch returns the server's new state — tile now reads cancelled.
+    expect(find.text('CANCELLED'), findsOneWidget);
+    expect(find.text('UPCOMING'), findsNothing);
+    // A cancelled trip offers archive, not cancel.
+    expect(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Archive'), findsNWidgets(2));
+    expect(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Cancel trip'), findsNothing);
+  });
+
+  testWidgets('archive clears a terminal trip to ARCHIVED', (tester) async {
+    await pumpTrips(tester);
+
+    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Archive'));
+    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
+
+    expect(fake.postedPaths, ['/bookings/2/archive']);
+    expect(find.text('ARCHIVED'), findsOneWidget);
+    // The archived tile shows no further actions; the live trip still can
+    // be cancelled.
+    expect(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Archive'), findsNothing);
+    expect(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Cancel trip'), findsOneWidget);
+  });
+
+  testWidgets('a failed cancel keeps the trip and surfaces the error',
+      (tester) async {
+    await pumpTrips(tester);
+    fake.actionError = ApiException(
+      kind: ApiFailureKind.server,
+      statusCode: 500,
+      message: 'Guides Nepal is having trouble right now. Please try again.',
+    );
+
+    await cancelFirstTrip(tester);
+
+    expect(
+      find.text('Guides Nepal is having trouble right now. Please try again.'),
+      findsOneWidget,
+    );
+    // Unchanged on screen and on the server.
+    expect(find.text('UPCOMING'), findsOneWidget);
+    expect(fake.server.first['status'], 'upcoming');
+    await drainSnackbars(tester);
+
+    // Retry succeeds once the server recovers.
+    fake.actionError = null;
+    await cancelFirstTrip(tester);
+    expect(find.text('CANCELLED'), findsOneWidget);
+    expect(fake.postedPaths, hasLength(2));
+  });
+
+  testWidgets('only one action request leaves the app while in flight',
+      (tester) async {
+    await pumpTrips(tester);
+    final gate = Completer<void>();
+    fake.actionGate = gate;
+
+    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, 'Cancel trip'));
+    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
+    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(FilledButton, 'Cancel trip'));
+    await tester.pump();
+    expect(fake.postedPaths, ['/bookings/1/cancel']);
+
+    // The tile's button is in its loading state (label swapped for a
+    // spinner, so find it by the label property); a second tap is a no-op.
+    final tileAction = find.byWidgetPredicate(
+      (w) => w is AppButton && w.label == 'Cancel trip',
+    );
+    expect(tester.widget<AppButton>(tileAction).loading, isTrue);
+    await tester.tap(tileAction);
+    await tester.pump();
+
+    gate.complete();
+    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
+
+    expect(fake.postedPaths, ['/bookings/1/cancel']); // still exactly one
+    expect(find.text('CANCELLED'), findsOneWidget);
+  });
+
+  testWidgets('empty trips state invites the traveler to explore',
+      (tester) async {
+    await pumpTrips(tester, server: []);
+
+    expect(find.text('No trips booked yet'), findsOneWidget);
+
+    await tester.tap(find.widgetWithText(AppButton, AppStrings.exploreExperiences));
+    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
+    expect(find.text('explore-screen'), findsOneWidget);
+  });
+}

## Quality gates (all run on this machine, 2026-10-21)

Run locally:

```bash
cd mobile
flutter pub get
flutter analyze
flutter test
flutter build apk --debug
```

## Test inventory

| File | Tests | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| `test/widget_test.dart` | 5 | Brand copy; formatters (`$50` vs `$49.50`, `/ person`, plural counts); `BookingStatus` parsing + `canCancel`; experience parsing (populated and minimal rows) |
| `test/widget_components_test.dart` | 11 | Shared widgets: experience/guide cards, save heart, chips, button states |
| `test/sign_in_validation_test.dart` | 4 | Sign-in form validation and submit gating |
| `test/booking_flow_test.dart` | 11 | Availability check, single non-idempotent `POST /bookings/`, duplicate-tap guard, confirmation routing |
| `test/trips_actions_test.dart` | 7 | Trips list; cancel (with confirmation) and archive against a stateful fake server; error + retry; one request in flight; empty state |
| `test/favorites_state_test.dart` | 4 | Optimistic bookmark toggle and revert on rejection |
| `test/app_router_redirect_test.dart` | 12 | Redirect guard: splash hold, signed-out allow-list, signed-in bounce, traveler/guide role guard incl. the listing editor |
| `test/guide_listing_editor_test.dart` | 16 | `ListingDraft` validation vs the server schema + JSON shape; create, edit, pause, delete, server rejection, missing listing; guide workspace card actions; onboarding envelope parsing |

## What's deliberately mocked vs real

Tests are hermetic: no live backend, no network, no production accounts.

- Pure Dart tests cover models, formatters and validation.
- Widget tests inject a fake `ApiClient` (`apiClientProvider` override) and a
  fake `AuthController`. The fakes hold **server-side state** and apply the
  request payloads, so the real repositories (`BookingRepository`,
  `GuideRepository`, …) and model parsers run unmodified — a status flip or a
  created listing proven in a test is the one the backend contract defines.

## Known gaps (not yet automated)

- Integration tests (`integration_test/`) for startup → sign-in → explore →
  detail → booking: need a seeded local backend; not run here.
- Golden/screenshot tests for visual regressions.
- Guide status-update composer and onboarding wizard have no UI yet, so no
  tests (see `api-gaps.md`).

These are honest gaps; none of the passing claims above substitute for them.

## Regression rules

- Never delete or weaken a test to make a change pass.
- Every fix must keep `flutter analyze` at zero and `flutter test` green.

- **New editor screen** — [listing_editor_screen.dart](mobile/lib/features/guide_tools/listing_editor_screen.dart) handles create and edit in one form: title, category chips (trekking/tour/specialized), city, area, duration, difficulty chips, price, max group size, description, itinerary, meeting point, a "visible to travellers" switch, and delete for existing listings. Reached from `/guide/listing/new` and `/guide/listing/:id`; it loads the listing from the guide's own `GET /guide/listings` rather than router `extra`, so a cold deep link works, and an id the guide doesn't own shows "This listing is no longer available." instead of a blank form.
- **Offline validation that matches the server** — `ListingDraft` in [guide_models.dart](mobile/lib/features/guide_tools/guide_models.dart) mirrors the `GuideListingCreate`/`GuideListingUpdate` limits (3–160 title, 10–5000 description, 1–100 guests, non-negative price, optional-field lengths) and serializes to the snake_case body the API expects, with empty optionals sent as `null`. Server 422s still map back onto the offending field, and a rejection keeps every typed value so the guide can retry.
- **Workspace wiring** — [guide_shell.dart](mobile/lib/features/guide_tools/guide_shell.dart): the Listings tab gains a "New listing" header action and each card gets Edit / Pause–Resume / Capacity; the empty state finally offers "Create a listing". Pausing patches `is_active` and the card refetches, so the "Paused" chip reflects server truth. Returns `true` only when the server state changed, so lists don't reload after a back-out.
- **Route guard** — [app_router.dart](mobile/lib/app/router/app_router.dart) now scopes the role guard to `/guide` *and* `/guide/listing*`, leaving `/guide/:id` profiles public for travellers.

**Two pre-existing bugs fixed along the way:**
- `fetchOnboarding()` parsed the `{onboarding, completed}` envelope as if it were the profile, so every field came back empty; it now unwraps it and treats `onboarding: null` (a guide who never onboarded) as an empty profile rather than an error.
- `_ListingsTabState._reload` did `setState(() => _future = …)`, whose closure returns a `Future` — an assertion in debug builds whenever the list was refreshed. It now computes the future first and assigns it in a block body.

**Verified:** `flutter analyze` → No issues found; `flutter test` → **70/70 passed** (18 new); `flutter build apk --debug` → built. The new [guide_listing_editor_test.dart](mobile/test/guide_listing_editor_test.dart) uses a stateful fake API, so the real `GuideRepository` and `GuideListing.fromJson` run unmodified — it drives the actual form (typing, chip taps, switch, delete confirmation), checks the outgoing payloads, the pop result the workspace depends on, and the pause→"Paused" refetch round trip. Docs updated: [api-gaps.md](mobile/docs/api-gaps.md), [api-integration.md](mobile/docs/api-integration.md), [architecture.md](mobile/docs/architecture.md), and [testing.md](mobile/docs/testing.md) (which still claimed 5 tests and listed now-covered gaps).

Everything remains uncommitted on disk; `mobile/` is untracked in git as before, and I haven't staged or committed anything.

The other gap the API already supports is a guide's public profile: onboarding (display name, expertise, cities, languages, bio, default group size) is wired and now parses correctly, but there's no screen for a guide to fill it in.

      v is List ? v.whereType<String>().toList(growable: false) : const [];

  /// than hidden.
  String get typeLabel => updateType.isEmpty
      ? 'Update'
      : '${updateType[0].toUpperCase()}${updateType.substring(1)}';

  /// `6/8 spots` for a capacity note, otherwise `null`. A half-filled pair
  /// (the server allows either alone) is shown as just what is known.
  String? get capacityLabel {
    final current = currentCapacity;
    final max = maxCapacity;
    if (current == null && max == null) return null;
    if (current != null && max != null) return '$current/$max spots';
    if (max != null) return 'Up to $max spots';
    return '$current spots taken';
  }

+
+/// The traveller's "my city": which city's local updates they see on Home.
+///
+/// Defaults to [kCities.first] (Kathmandu) so Home always resolves to a
+/// valid municipal city with zero setup. Persisted in secure storage —
+/// like [TokenStorage]'s session values this is a one-line preference, and
+/// keeping it here means no second storage channel to manage. The provider
+/// never throws: a storage failure just falls back to the default for the
+/// session instead of breaking Home.
+class HomeCityStore extends StateNotifier<String> {
+  HomeCityStore({FlutterSecureStorage? storage, String? initial})
+      : _storage = storage ??
+            const FlutterSecureStorage(
+              aOptions: AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences: true),
+            ),
+        super(initial ?? kCities.first) {
+    _restore();
+  }
+
+  static const _kHomeCity = 'gn_home_city';
+
+  final FlutterSecureStorage _storage;
+
+  Future<void> _restore() async {
+    try {
+      final saved = await _storage.read(key: _kHomeCity);
+      if (saved != null && kCities.contains(saved)) {
+        state = saved;
+      }
+    } on Exception {
+      // Best effort only — keep the default.
+    }
+  }
+
+  Future<void> setCity(String city) async {
+    if (!kCities.contains(city) || city == state) return;
+    state = city;
+    try {
+      await _storage.write(key: _kHomeCity, value: city);
+    } on Exception {
+      // Preference persistence is non-critical.
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+final homeCityProvider = StateNotifierProvider<HomeCityStore, String>(
+  (ref) => HomeCityStore(),
+);
+
+/// Home feed key, differentiated per city so Riverpod caches each city's
+/// feed independently and a city flip re-fetches without a manual reload.
+final cityUpdatesFeedProvider = FutureProvider.autoDispose
+    .family<List<CityUpdate>, String>((ref, city) {
+  return ref.watch(experienceRepositoryProvider).fetchCityUpdates(city);
+});

+        ``host_guides`` ever creates one, and no seed does). Scoping by city
+        is also what travellers actually navigate by.
+
+        An update qualifies when it:
+
+        * belongs to a guide who lists [city] on their onboarding profile, or
+          is attached to an active listing in [city];
+        * is still active (a guide can unpublish an update without deleting it);
+        * is not stale — a dated update must not be past its day, and an
+          undated one must be less than [max_age_days] old, so a traveller
+          never reads "two spots left" about a trip that already left;
+        * is not an internal ``booking`` note, which is written for the guide's
+          own workflow rather than for travellers.
+
+        Rows are fetched newest-first and truncated once [limit] matches are
+        collected, so the limit applies to visible updates rather than to
+        candidates.

+            if row.event_date is not None:
+                stamp = row.event_date
+                if stamp.tzinfo is None:

+            if row.created_at is None:

+                "cities": cities,
+            })

Provide a mobile support experience for:

- Help and FAQ
- Contact/support entry point
- Ticket submission
- Ticket status where supported
- Booking-related help
- Error reporting instructions

Reuse existing support functionality.

Do not build an unrelated support database.

---

# 21. MAPS AND LOCATION

Use maps where they genuinely improve travel planning.

Possible functionality:

- Destination maps
- Experience locations
- Meeting points
- Directions
- Map/list browsing
- Nearby experiences, if supported

Choose a suitable map provider after evaluating:

- Coverage in Nepal
- Pricing
- Licensing
- API key restrictions
- Android support
- iOS support
- Offline needs
- Privacy implications

Request location permission only when necessary.

The application must still work when location permission is denied.

Do not send location data unnecessarily.

Never imply that an approximate location is precise.

---

# 22. NOTIFICATIONS AND DEEP LINKS

Create notification infrastructure for relevant events:

- Booking updates
- Booking confirmation
- Host messages
- Personalized offers
- Payment status
- Trip reminders
- Cancellations
- Support updates

Use a suitable notification service and native platform configuration.

Do not assume push notifications work merely because the Flutter package is installed.

Verify:

- Android configuration
- iOS/APNs configuration
- Permission flow
- Device token registration
- Backend token storage
- Notification delivery
- Logout and token lifecycle
- Deep links

Potential deep-link destinations:

```text
guidesnepal://experience/{id}
guidesnepal://host/{id}
guidesnepal://guide/{id}
guidesnepal://booking/{id}
guidesnepal://trip/{id}
guidesnepal://conversation/{id}
```

Choose the final scheme after inspecting the existing domain and deployment configuration.

Support HTTPS app links/universal links where configured.

Every deep link must validate authentication and authorization.

---

# 23. OFFLINE SUPPORT AND NETWORK RESILIENCE

Travelers may have unreliable internet connections.

Design useful offline behavior without compromising transactional correctness.

Potentially cache:

- Recently viewed experiences
- Destination content
- Non-sensitive preferences
- Saved display data
- Upcoming trip details where appropriate

Clearly distinguish cached data from fresh server data.

Handle:

- Offline
- Reconnecting
- Synchronizing
- Failed requests
- Stale data
- Retry

Never present stale availability as current.

Never report a booking or payment as completed without server confirmation.

Do not queue financial transactions for blind execution when connectivity returns.

Define conflict handling before implementing synchronization.

---

# 24. INTERNATIONALIZATION AND CURRENCY

Design for international travelers.

Prepare localization infrastructure for:

- English initially
- Additional languages in the future
- Locale-aware date formatting
- Time-zone-aware booking times
- Currency formatting

Do not hardcode currency symbols throughout widgets.

Use backend-provided pricing and currency information where available.

Do not convert prices using invented exchange rates.

The UI must distinguish display formatting from actual transaction currency.

Use Nepal's local time appropriately when displaying local experience times, while preserving the timezone returned or defined by the backend.

---

# 25. ACCESSIBILITY

Meet practical accessibility standards.

Include:

- Semantic labels
- Screen reader support
- Adequate contrast
- Scalable text
- Keyboard and focus support where relevant
- Accessible form validation
- Minimum practical touch targets
- Reduced-motion considerations
- Clear error announcements

Do not rely on color alone to communicate booking status or errors.

Test important flows using accessibility tools and screen readers where possible.

---

# 26. PERFORMANCE AND IMAGE OPTIMIZATION

Optimize the app for real devices, including mid-range Android phones.

Requirements:

- Paginated lists
- Lazy loading
- Image caching
- Appropriate image sizes
- Efficient list rendering
- Minimal unnecessary widget rebuilds
- Request cancellation
- Debounced search
- Memory-conscious image galleries
- Smooth scrolling
- Efficient state management
- Clear loading states

Avoid downloading full-resolution images for small cards.

Use server-side image transformations or a compatible image CDN if available.

Do not add an image-processing backend service without evidence that it is needed.

Measure performance and investigate bottlenecks instead of assuming the app is optimized.

---

# 27. ERROR HANDLING AND LOGGING

Build a consistent error-handling layer.

Handle:

- Network failure
- Timeout
- Invalid response
- Authentication failure
- Expired session
- Permission denial
- Validation failure
- Booking conflict
- Unavailable experience
- Payment failure
- AI failure
- Upload failure
- Offline mode

User-facing messages must be understandable and actionable.

Never expose:

- Stack traces
- Internal server errors
- Secrets
- Tokens
- Database details
- Private user information

Use structured logging with sensitive data redacted.

Never log passwords, authentication tokens, payment secrets, or unnecessary personal data.

---

# 28. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

Apply security throughout the application.

Requirements:

- Secure token storage
- HTTPS for production API requests
- Server-side authorization
- Input validation
- Safe error handling
- Secure deep-link handling
- Sensitive-data minimization
- Secure file-upload handling
- Appropriate session expiration behavior
- Dependency review
- Environment separation
- Safe logging
- Privacy-conscious analytics

Do not embed server secrets in the Flutter application.

Do not place database credentials or privileged API keys in Dart source code.

A public mobile application cannot safely conceal secrets merely by putting them in environment files during compilation.

Use backend-mediated operations for privileged actions.

Do not rely on obfuscation as a replacement for server-side security.

Do not introduce certificate pinning without a documented threat model and a reliable certificate-rotation strategy.

Review account deletion, privacy, and consent requirements before release.

@app.on_event("startup")
def ensure_database_schema() -> None:
    """Create database tables if they don't exist yet.

    This guarantees the `users` (and other) tables exist wherever the app can
    reach the configured database, so registrations actually have somewhere to
    be stored. Failures are logged (not fatal) so the app still boots and can
    report a clear error on DB-dependent requests instead of crashing.
    """
    try:
        Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
        inspector = inspect(engine)
        booking_columns = {column["name"] for column in inspector.get_columns("bookings")}
        if "guide_user_id" not in booking_columns:
            with engine.begin() as connection:
                connection.execute(text("ALTER TABLE bookings ADD COLUMN guide_user_id INTEGER"))
        logger.info("Database schema verified/created successfully.")
    except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover - depends on DB availability
        logger.error(f"Could not create/verify database schema: {e}")

+import 'package:flutter_riverpod/flutter_riverpod.dart';
+import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
+
+import 'package:guides_nepal/app/app.dart';

+/// Auth state that is already signed in — bypasses secure storage and the
+/// network so the first frame resolves straight to `/home`.
+class _SignedInAuth extends AuthController {
+  @override
+  AuthState build() => const AuthState(
+        status: AuthStatus.authenticated,
+        user: AppUser(

+          email: 'traveler@guides-nepal.com',

+          lastName: 'Traveler',

+
+void main() {

+    // pending HTTP futures never settle in the test environment.

+      findsOneWidget,
+      reason: 'Home body should render; a thrown framework assertion '

+    );
+  });
+}

## What was broken, and what's fixed

**1. Sign-in was impossible in the browser — two independent causes**
- The backend's CORS allowlist (`backend/.env`) only trusted the React dev origins (5174–5176), so the browser preflight from the Flutter web server on 8085 returned **400** and every API call died as "Could not reach Guides Nepal." Added `http://localhost:8085` and `http://127.0.0.1:8085`.
- The web build, with no `API_BASE_URL` define, silently pointed at **production** (`kIsWeb` → `onrender.com`). The dev server must run with `--dart-define=API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/v1`.

**2. Sessions died silently after 30 minutes** — the backend minted refresh tokens (7-day life) but had **no refresh endpoint**, and the app never used the stored token; `restoreSession` cleared secure storage the moment `/profile/me` answered 401. Now:
- [auth.py](backend/app/api/v1/auth.py) exposes `POST /auth/refresh`: validates the token is type `refresh`, checks the user is active, rotates the pair, and rejects access tokens, tampered tokens and inactive users with 401.
- [auth_repository.dart](mobile/lib/features/auth/auth_repository.dart) retries with the refresh token before signing out; only a rejected refresh clears the session.
- Covered by [test_auth.py](backend/tests/test_auth.py) (4 tests) and [auth_refresh_test.dart](mobile/test/auth_refresh_test.dart) (6 tests), and [api-gaps.md](mobile/docs/api-gaps.md) now documents the built contract and the one remaining gap (in-session 401 retry).

**3. Explore cards showed red "OVERFLOWED BY 9/54 PIXELS" ribbons** — the star + full "(156 reviews)" + "$40 / person" didn't fit a 2-column grid cell. [experience_card.dart](mobile/lib/shared/widgets/experience_card.dart) now scales the rating group down as one unit and shows compact counts ("(45)", "1.2k"), with the full "N reviews" phrase preserved in the accessibility label ([formatters.dart](mobile/lib/core/utils/formatters.dart) gained `reviewCountShort`).

## Verified live in the browser (app :8085 → API :8001)
Sign-in → `#/home` with greeting; Home updates feed shows real `/updates` data (Mingma Sherpa, 17h ago); Explore lists 12 experiences and the Kathmandu filter fires `GET /experiences?city=Kathmandu` (3 results) with no overflow; Contact pre-fills the account, `POST /inquiries` returns **201** and the "Message sent" screen appears; FAQ renders all 8 questions with working accordions; **a full page reload while signed in stays on `#/home`**. The refresh endpoint was also exercised over HTTP: login → refresh (rotated pair, new token accepted on `/profile/me`) → access-token-as-refresh 401 → garbage 401.

**Checks:** mobile `flutter analyze` clean, **120 tests pass**; backend **148 passed**. Three backend failures pre-date this work and are environmental: the two OAuth-start tests need `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`FACEBOOK_CLIENT_ID` in `.env`, and the AI test needs an external service.

/// Attaches the bearer token to every request and renews it silently.
///
/// When a request returns 401 the interceptor exchanges the stored refresh
/// token at `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` and replays the original request
/// once with the new access token. Refreshes are single-flight: parallel
/// 401s share one exchange, so a burst of requests never hammers the
/// endpoint. Only when the refresh itself is rejected (or no refresh token
/// is stored) does [onUnauthorized] fire and the caller see
/// [ApiFailureKind.unauthorized].
class AuthInterceptor extends Interceptor {
  AuthInterceptor({TokenStorage? tokenStorage, Dio? refreshDio})
      : _tokenStorage = tokenStorage ?? TokenStorage(),
        _refreshDio = refreshDio ??
            Dio(
              BaseOptions(
                baseUrl: AppConfig.baseUrl,
                connectTimeout: const Duration(seconds: 15),
                receiveTimeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
                sendTimeout: const Duration(seconds: 20),
                headers: const {
                  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
                  'Accept': 'application/json',
                },
              ),
            );

  final TokenStorage _tokenStorage;

  /// Dedicated client for the refresh exchange. It carries no interceptor,
  /// so a rejected refresh can never recurse back into this one.
  final Dio _refreshDio;

  /// The client that issued the request — set by [ApiClient] so a refreshed
  /// request can be replayed.
  Dio? _dio;

  Future<bool>? _refreshing;

  /// Marks a replayed request so a second 401 cannot trigger a loop.
  static const _retryKey = 'auth_retry_after_refresh';

  /// Invoked when a 401 cannot be recovered — the router clears the session
  /// and redirects to sign-in.
  void Function()? onUnauthorized;

  String? _cachedToken;

  /// Pre-seed the token after login to avoid an async read on hot paths.
  void setToken(String? token) {
    _cachedToken = token;
    if (token != null) _tokenStorage.saveAccessToken(token);
  }

  /// Called once by [ApiClient] so the interceptor can replay requests.
  void attachDio(Dio dio) => _dio = dio;

  Future<void> primeFromStorage() async {
    _cachedToken ??= await _tokenStorage.readAccessToken();
  }

  @override
  Future<void> onRequest(
    RequestOptions options,
    RequestInterceptorHandler handler,
  ) async {
    final token = _cachedToken ?? await _tokenStorage.readAccessToken();
    _cachedToken = token;
    if (token != null && token.isNotEmpty) {
      options.headers['Authorization'] = 'Bearer $token';
    }
    handler.next(options);
  }

  @override
  void onError(DioException err, ErrorInterceptorHandler handler) {
    final options = err.requestOptions;
    final isRefreshCall = options.path.contains('/auth/refresh');
    final alreadyRetried = options.extra[_retryKey] == true;

    if (err.response?.statusCode == 401 && !isRefreshCall && !alreadyRetried) {
      _recoverFromUnauthorized(err, handler);
      return;
    }

    if (err.response?.statusCode == 401) {
      // The refresh exchange itself was rejected (or the replay also saw a
      // 401): the session is genuinely over.
      onUnauthorized?.call();
    }
    // Normalized by ApiClient.mapDioException at the call site.
    handler.next(err);
  }

  /// Refreshes the session, then replays [err]'s request exactly once.
  Future<void> _recoverFromUnauthorized(
    DioException err,
    ErrorInterceptorHandler handler,
  ) async {
    final refreshed = await _refreshOnce();
    final dio = _dio;
    if (!refreshed || dio == null) {
      onUnauthorized?.call();
      handler.next(err);
      return;
    }

    final options = err.requestOptions..extra[_retryKey] = true;
    if (_cachedToken != null) {
      options.headers['Authorization'] = 'Bearer $_cachedToken';
    }
    try {
      handler.resolve(await dio.fetch(options));
    } on DioException catch (retryError) {
      if (retryError.response?.statusCode == 401) {
        onUnauthorized?.call();
      }
      handler.next(retryError);
    } catch (_) {
      handler.next(err);
    }
  }

  /// One refresh exchange shared by every concurrent 401.
  Future<bool> _refreshOnce() {
    final inFlight = _refreshing;
    if (inFlight != null) return inFlight;
    final future = _performRefresh().whenComplete(() => _refreshing = null);
    _refreshing = future;
    return future;
  }

  Future<bool> _performRefresh() async {
    final refreshToken = await _tokenStorage.readRefreshToken();
    if (refreshToken == null || refreshToken.isEmpty) return false;

    try {
      final res = await _refreshDio.post(
        '/auth/refresh',
        data: {'refresh_token': refreshToken},
      );
      final map = (res.data as Map).cast<String, dynamic>();
      final accessToken = map['access_token'] as String? ?? '';
      final nextRefresh = map['refresh_token'] as String? ?? '';
      final user = map['user'];
      if (accessToken.isEmpty) return false;

      _cachedToken = accessToken;
      if (user is Map && nextRefresh.isNotEmpty) {
        // Persist the rotated pair and identity together; a crash between
        // writes must not leave an access token without its refresh token.
        await _tokenStorage.saveSession(
          accessToken: accessToken,
          refreshToken: nextRefresh,
          userJson: jsonEncode(user),
        );
      } else {
        await _tokenStorage.saveAccessToken(accessToken);
      }
      return true;
    } catch (_) {
      return false;
    }
  }

  Future<void> clearSession() async {
    _cachedToken = null;
    await _tokenStorage.clear();
  }

  /// Exposed for tests: throws a normalized exception from a raw Dio error.
  static ApiException map(DioException e) => ApiClient.mapDioException(e);
}

/// In-memory [TokenStorage] — secure storage has no plugin in tests, and the
/// interceptor only uses the read/write/clear surface.
class _MemoryTokenStorage extends TokenStorage {
  final Map<String, String> data = {};

  @override
  Future<void> saveSession({
    required String accessToken,
    required String refreshToken,
    required String userJson,
  }) async {
    data['gn_access_token'] = accessToken;
    data['gn_refresh_token'] = refreshToken;
    data['gn_user_json'] = userJson;
  }

  @override
  Future<void> saveAccessToken(String token) async =>
      data['gn_access_token'] = token;

  @override
  Future<String?> readAccessToken() async => data['gn_access_token'];

  @override
  Future<String?> readRefreshToken() async => data['gn_refresh_token'];

  @override
  Future<String?> readUserJson() async => data['gn_user_json'];

  @override
  Future<void> clear() async => data.clear();
}

/// Dio transport stub: [respond] decides the reply (and may wait, so tests
/// can hold a response open and observe single-flight behaviour).
class _ScriptedAdapter implements HttpClientAdapter {
  _ScriptedAdapter(this.respond);

  final FutureOr<(int, Object?)> Function(RequestOptions options) respond;
  final List<String> requests = [];

  @override
  Future<ResponseBody> fetch(
    RequestOptions options,
    Stream<Uint8List>? requestStream,
    Future<void>? cancelFuture,
  ) async {
    requests.add(options.path);
    final (status, body) = await respond(options);
    return ResponseBody.fromString(
      body == null ? '' : jsonEncode(body),
      status,
      headers: {
        Headers.contentTypeHeader: [Headers.jsonContentType],
      },
    );
  }

  @override
  void close({bool force = false}) {}
}

Map<String, dynamic> _tokens({String access = 'new-access', String refresh = 'refresh-2'}) => {
      'access_token': access,
      'refresh_token': refresh,
      'token_type': 'bearer',
      'user': {
        'id': 7,
        'email': 'traveler@example.com',
        'firstName': 'Test',
        'lastName': 'Traveler',
        'role': 'traveler',
        'is_active': true,
      },
    };

class _Harness {
  _Harness({
    required FutureOr<(int, Object?)> Function(RequestOptions options) main,
    required FutureOr<(int, Object?)> Function(RequestOptions options) refresh,
    Map<String, String>? stored,
  }) {
    storage = _MemoryTokenStorage();
    if (stored != null) storage.data.addAll(stored);
    mainAdapter = _ScriptedAdapter(main);
    refreshAdapter = _ScriptedAdapter(refresh);
    final refreshDio = Dio(BaseOptions(baseUrl: 'http://api.test/api/v1'))
      ..httpClientAdapter = refreshAdapter;
    final dio = Dio(BaseOptions(baseUrl: 'http://api.test/api/v1'))
      ..httpClientAdapter = mainAdapter;
    client = ApiClient(
      dio: dio,
      authInterceptor:
          AuthInterceptor(tokenStorage: storage, refreshDio: refreshDio),
    );
    client.authInterceptor.onUnauthorized = () => unauthorizedCalls++;
  }

  late final _MemoryTokenStorage storage;
  late final _ScriptedAdapter mainAdapter;
  late final _ScriptedAdapter refreshAdapter;
  late final ApiClient client;
  int unauthorizedCalls = 0;
}

/// 401 until the rotated bearer token arrives, then 200.
FutureOr<(int, Object?)> _expiringEndpoint(RequestOptions options) {
  if (options.headers['Authorization'] == 'Bearer new-access') {
    return (200, {'email': 'traveler@example.com'});
  }
  return (401, {'detail': 'Access token expired'});
}

void main() {
  // TokenStorage constructs a FlutterSecureStorage, which needs the binding
  // before any platform channel is touched.
  TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();

  group('AuthInterceptor silent refresh', () {
    test('a 401 is refreshed and the original request replayed once', () async {
      final h = _Harness(
        main: _expiringEndpoint,
        refresh: (_) => (200, _tokens()),
        stored: {'gn_access_token': 'stale', 'gn_refresh_token': 'refresh-1'},
      );

      final res = await h.client.get('/profile/me');

      expect(res.statusCode, 200);
      expect((res.data as Map)['email'], 'traveler@example.com');
      expect(h.mainAdapter.requests.length, 2, reason: 'original + replay');
      expect(h.refreshAdapter.requests.single, contains('/auth/refresh'));
      expect(h.unauthorizedCalls, 0);
      expect(h.storage.data['gn_access_token'], 'new-access');
      expect(h.storage.data['gn_refresh_token'], 'refresh-2');
      expect(h.storage.data['gn_user_json'], contains('traveler@example.com'));
    });

    test('a rejected refresh signs the session out and surfaces 401', () async {
      final h = _Harness(
        main: (o) => (401, {'detail': 'Access token expired'}),
        refresh: (_) => (401, {'detail': 'Invalid refresh token'}),
        stored: {'gn_access_token': 'stale', 'gn_refresh_token': 'stale-too'},
      );

      Object? caught;
      try {
        await h.client.get('/profile/me');
      } catch (e) {
        caught = e;
      }

      expect(caught, isA<ApiException>());
      expect((caught as ApiException).kind, ApiFailureKind.unauthorized);
      expect(h.unauthorizedCalls, 1);
      expect(h.mainAdapter.requests.length, 1, reason: 'no replay');
      expect(h.refreshAdapter.requests.length, 1);
      // The failed exchange must not erase credentials mid-flight — the auth
      // layer decides when to clear storage.
      expect(h.storage.data['gn_refresh_token'], 'stale-too');
    });

    test('no stored refresh token means an immediate sign-out', () async {
      final h = _Harness(
        main: (o) => (401, {'detail': 'Access token expired'}),
        refresh: (_) => (200, _tokens()),
        stored: {'gn_access_token': 'stale'},
      );

      await expectLater(
        h.client.get('/profile/me'),
        throwsA(isA<ApiException>().having(
            (e) => e.kind, 'kind', ApiFailureKind.unauthorized)),
      );
      expect(h.refreshAdapter.requests, isEmpty);
      expect(h.unauthorizedCalls, 1);
    });

    test('parallel 401s share a single refresh exchange', () async {
      final gate = Completer<void>();
      final h = _Harness(
        main: _expiringEndpoint,
        refresh: (_) async {
          await gate.future;
          return (200, _tokens());
        },
        stored: {'gn_access_token': 'stale', 'gn_refresh_token': 'refresh-1'},
      );

      final first = h.client.get('/profile/me');
      final second = h.client.get('/profile/me');
      // Let both requests reach their 401s before the exchange resolves.
      await Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero);
      gate.complete();

      final responses = await Future.wait([first, second]);
      expect(responses.map((r) => r.statusCode), [200, 200]);
      expect(h.refreshAdapter.requests.length, 1,
          reason: 'one exchange for the whole burst');
      expect(h.unauthorizedCalls, 0);
    });

    test('a non-auth failure is never retried', () async {
      final h = _Harness(
        main: (o) => (500, {'detail': 'boom'}),
        refresh: (_) => (200, _tokens()),
        stored: {'gn_access_token': 'ok', 'gn_refresh_token': 'refresh-1'},
      );

      await expectLater(
        h.client.get('/profile/me'),
        throwsA(isA<ApiException>()
            .having((e) => e.kind, 'kind', ApiFailureKind.server)),
      );
      expect(h.mainAdapter.requests.length, 1);
      expect(h.refreshAdapter.requests, isEmpty);
      expect(h.unauthorizedCalls, 0);
    });
  });
}

## What changed

**[auth_interceptor.dart](mobile/lib/core/network/auth_interceptor.dart)** now recovers a 401 instead of ending the session:
- Exchanges the stored refresh token at `POST /auth/refresh` and **replays the original request once** with the rotated access token.
- Refreshes are **single-flight** — a burst of parallel 401s shares one exchange (the test holds the response open to prove it).
- The refresh uses its own interceptor-free Dio, so a rejected refresh can't recurse; a `_retryKey` marker on the replayed request prevents loops.
- Only when the refresh is rejected (or no refresh token exists) does `onUnauthorized` fire — the existing sign-out path.
- The rotated pair and user identity are persisted together via one `saveSession`, so a crash can't leave a token without its refresh token.

**[api_client.dart](mobile/lib/core/network/api_client.dart)** wires the interceptor to its client (`attachDio`) and the class doc now states the retry contract honestly: the only automatic retry is the post-refresh replay, which is safe because a 401 means the server rejected the request before executing it.

def logout(request: RefreshRequest, db: Session = Depends(get_db)) -> dict:
    """Revoke the presented refresh token.

    Best-effort and idempotent: it always answers 200 so signing out can
    never fail in the client, and an already-expired or unreadable token is
    simply ignored (it cannot be used anyway). The token's `jti` is recorded
    so `/auth/refresh` rejects it from now on; the access token already
    issued stays valid until its short expiry by design.
    """
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(
            request.refresh_token,
            settings.SECRET_KEY,
            algorithms=[settings.ALGORITHM],
        )
    except JWTError:
        return {"status": "ok"}

    if payload.get("type") != "refresh":
        return {"status": "ok"}

    jti = payload.get("jti")
    exp = payload.get("exp")
    if jti and exp:
        now = datetime.utcnow()
        expires_at = datetime.utcfromtimestamp(exp)
        if expires_at > now:
            if (
                db.query(RevokedToken).filter(RevokedToken.jti == jti).first()
                is None
            ):
                db.add(RevokedToken(jti=jti, expires_at=expires_at))
            # Prune rows for tokens that have expired anyway.
            db.query(RevokedToken).filter(RevokedToken.expires_at < now).delete()
            db.commit()

    return {"status": "ok"}

## 4. Sign-out revocation — IMPLEMENTED (refresh tokens)

- **Contract:** `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` → `{refresh_token}` → 200
  `{status: "ok"}`. Always 200 (idempotent, and an unreadable/expired token
  is ignored), so a client can sign out offline-safe.
- **Mechanism:** every refresh token carries a unique `jti`; logout records
  it in `revoked_tokens` (pruned as entries expire), and
  `/auth/refresh` rejects a revoked `jti` with 401. Revocation is
  per-session: other devices' refresh tokens keep working.
- **Mobile behavior:** `AuthRepository.logout` posts the stored refresh
  token before clearing storage; failure (offline) still signs out locally.
- **Residual risk:** access tokens are stateless JWTs, so one already issued
  stays valid until its expiry (≤30 min). Full instant revocation would
  require a token-version check on every request.

## Server-side logout now revokes tokens

**Backend**
- Every refresh token now carries a unique `jti` ([security.py](backend/app/core/security.py)).
- New table [token_revocation.py](backend/app/models/token_revocation.py) (`revoked_tokens`: `jti`, `expires_at`, `revoked_at`) with migration [a7b1c2d3e4f5_create_revoked_tokens_table.py](backend/migrations/versions/a7b1c2d3e4f5_create_revoked_tokens_table.py) on the current head; startup `create_all` also covers it.
- `POST /auth/logout` ([auth.py](backend/app/api/v1/auth.py)) records the token's `jti` and prunes expired rows. It is idempotent and always answers 200 — an unreadable or already-expired token is ignored — so a client can sign out regardless of state.
- `POST /auth/refresh` rejects a revoked `jti` with **401 "Refresh token has been revoked"**.

**Client**
- [auth_repository.dart](mobile/lib/features/auth/auth_repository.dart): `logout()` posts the stored refresh token before clearing storage; a failed call (offline) still signs out locally.
- [auth_interceptor.dart](mobile/lib/core/network/auth_interceptor.dart): `/auth/refresh` and `/auth/logout` are auth-lifecycle calls — a 401 there never triggers another refresh or a recursive logout.

## Verified live
- **HTTP:** refresh before logout `200` → `/auth/logout 200` → refresh `401 Refresh token has been revoked` → a second session's refresh still `200` → repeat logout `200`. The revoked row exists in `revoked_tokens` with the right expiry.
- **UI:** signing out from Profile hit `POST /api/v1/auth/logout → 200` (CORS preflight passed) and landed on `#/onboarding`; the fresh session's token was recorded.
- One nuance found and documented: the first UI sign-out carried a refresh token minted *before* `jti` support, so it was ignored by design — such tokens can't be revoked and expire on their own (≤7 days).

**Checks:** backend **153 passed** (the same 3 pre-existing environment failures: two OAuth tests need client IDs, one AI test needs an external service); mobile analyzer clean, **128 tests pass** (5 logout/refresh-revocation tests added: revocation, per-session isolation, idempotency, garbage token, rotated-token validity, plus three client logout tests).
